Assume for contradiction that \(x>1\). Taking \(n=2\), for which \(\varphi(2)=1\), gives
\[
4y^2+1\mid x-1.
\]
Choose a prime \(p\mid 4y^2+1\). The number \(4y^2+1\) is odd and is not divisible by \(3\), since \(4y^2+1\equiv y^2+1\not\equiv0\pmod3\). Hence \(p\ge5\). Let
\[
a=v_p(x-1)\ge1
\]
and choose an integer \(k>a\).

Set \(f(T)=y^2T^2+1\). Since \(f(2)\equiv0\pmod p\) and
\[
f'(2)=4y^2\not\equiv0\pmod p,
\]
Hensel lifting gives an integer \(r\) such that
\[
r\equiv2\pmod p,\qquad f(r)\equiv0\pmod{p^k}.
\]
Thus \(s=-r\) also satisfies \(f(s)\equiv0\pmod{p^k}\), with \(s\equiv p-2\pmod p\).

Let \(b=(p-1)^2\). Since \(b-1=p(p-2)\), we have \(v_p(b-1)=1\). By LTE, for every positive integer \(m\),
\[
v_p(b^m-1)=1+v_p(m).
\]
Therefore \(b\) has order \(p^{k-1}\) modulo \(p^k\). Hence it generates the subgroup of units congruent to \(1\pmod p\), which has order \(p^{k-1}\).

Because \(s(p-2)^{-1}\equiv1\pmod p\), there exists \(t\ge0\) such that
\[
b^t\equiv s(p-2)^{-1}\pmod{p^k}.
\]
Define
\[
n=(p-2)(p-1)^{2t}=(p-2)b^t.
\]
Then \(n\equiv s\pmod{p^k}\), so
\[
p^k\mid n^2y^2+1.
\]
Every prime divisor \(q\) of \(n\) divides either \(p-2\) or \(p-1\), and therefore \(q<p\). From
\[
\varphi(n)=\prod_{q^e\parallel n}q^{e-1}(q-1),
\]
it follows that \(p\nmid\varphi(n)\).

The hypothesis now gives
\[
n^2y^2+1\\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1,
\]
and hence \(p^k\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1\). But since \(p\) is odd, \(p\mid x-1\), and \(p\nmid\varphi(n)\), LTE yields
\[
v_p\!\left(x^{\varphi(n)}-1\right)
=v_p(x-1)+v_p(\varphi(n))=a<k,
\]
contradicting \(p^k\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1\).

Thus \(x>1\) is impossible. Since \(x\) is a positive integer, \(x=1\).
input.theorem:
Let \( x \) and \( y \) be positive integers. If for each positive integer \( n \) we have that

\[
(n y)^{2}+1 \mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1
\]

prove that \( x=1 \).
